task: As CTO of a 40-person startup, I need to tell everyone that the December offsite in Austin is cancelled because of budget cuts after our funding round came in smaller than planned. We're going to do a virtual holiday lunch instead and I want to acknowledge people were excited about it. Write the Slack announcement, about 150 words, direct but not cold.
rewrite:
ambition: A top internal-comms lead would open with the decision in the first line, give the real reason in one plain sentence with no spin, and end with a concrete next step so nobody has to DM to ask what happens now.

agency: The rawest material is the original offsite announcement thread in Slack, which shows what people said they were looking forward to. It isn't in reach here, so the draft works from what you've said: the offsite was anticipated, the funding round came in smaller than planned, and a virtual lunch replaces it.

acceleration: Use the bad-news-first structure (decision, reason, acknowledgment, next step) in short Slack-native paragraphs with no headers, and give the new plan a specific date and time slot.

accuracy: Nothing outside the model can verify the words. The closest proxy is to have one colleague, such as your head of people, read it cold and say in one sentence what's cancelled, why, and what happens next. If they can't, the draft is unclear. Also confirm that the funding framing is something leadership has agreed to share.

deeper task:
Write a Slack announcement of about 150 words from me, the CTO of a 40-person startup, telling the whole company that the December offsite in Austin is cancelled because of budget cuts after our funding round came in smaller than planned. We're doing a virtual holiday lunch instead. Tone is direct but not cold. Open with the cancellation in the first sentence. State the reason in one honest sentence, without blaming anyone or dressing it up. Acknowledge that people were excited about the offsite and that this is a real disappointment, in words that sound like a person and not a press release. Then introduce the virtual lunch as the replacement, with a blank for the date and time that I'll fill in, and close by inviting people to bring questions to me directly. Use short paragraphs, no headers, and no more than one emoji, if any. Do not invent numbers, dates, or details I haven't given.

answers.plain:
**Slack announcement:**

Hi team,

I have some disappointing news: we're cancelling the December offsite in Austin.

Our funding round came in smaller than we planned, and we're making budget cuts to extend our runway. The offsite was one of the things we had to give up. I know many of you were looking forward to it, and I was too. I wish I had better news.

To still mark the end of the year together, we'll hold a virtual holiday lunch in December. We'll cover the cost of your meal, and we'll set aside the time to catch up, celebrate what we've built this year, and have some fun. I'll share the date and details soon.

Thank you for your understanding, and for everything you've done this year. If you have questions or concerns, please reach out to me directly or bring them to our next all-hands. I'm happy to talk through any of it.

[Your name]

---

That's about 160 words. A few notes:

- I wrote that the company will cover meals for the lunch. That's an assumption, so change or remove it if it isn't the plan.
- I said you'll share details soon and mentioned the all-hands. Adjust these if the timing differs.
- If you'd like it to be more direct, cut "I wish I had better news" and the closing offer to talk.
answers.nudge:
**Slack announcement**

Hi all, I have some disappointing news: we're cancelling the December offsite in Austin.

Our funding round came in smaller than we planned, so we're cutting back on spending to protect our runway. The offsite was one of the things we had to cut. I know many of you were excited about it, and I was too. I didn't make this decision lightly.

Instead, we'll hold a virtual holiday lunch on [date] at [time]. [We'll cover a meal for everyone, so you can order something great wherever you are.] It won't be Austin, but I want it to be a real chance to celebrate the year together.

If you have questions about the decision, ask in this thread or grab time with me directly. I'll also cover it at the next all-hands.

Thank you for your understanding, and for everything you've put into this year.

**Notes**
- **Bracketed items:** Fill in the date and time. I added the meal line as a suggestion, so keep it only if you'll fund it. A stipend makes the lunch feel like a real replacement rather than a consolation prize.
- **Why the reason is stated plainly:** In a 40-person company, people will guess at the cause if you're vague, and the guesses are usually worse than the truth. "Smaller than planned" is honest without alarming anyone. If the runway line overstates things, change it to match your actual situation.
- **Before posting:** Tell your leadership team first so they can answer questions right away. Post it early in the week and in the morning, so people can react and ask questions during working hours.

Team, we're cancelling the December offsite in Austin. Our funding round came in smaller than we planned, and we have to cut costs, so the trip isn't something we can afford.

I know a lot of you were looking forward to it, and I was too. Getting everyone together in one place is one of the things I enjoy most about this company. This is a real disappointment, and I'm sorry to be the one delivering it.

Instead, we're going to have a virtual holiday lunch on [DATE] at [TIME]. It won't be Austin, but I want us to still take a moment to celebrate the year together and spend some time that isn't about work.

If you have questions about the decision, the budget, or anything else, bring them to me directly. You can DM me or grab time on my calendar. I'll give you straight answers.

That comes to about 150 words. I didn't add an emoji, and I didn't state any figures or details beyond what you gave me. The "DM me or grab time on my calendar" line is a small addition, so cut it if you'd rather not offer that.
